findings.title: Form fields without a visible, programmatic label

impact.who: Screen-reader users hear only "edit text"; voice-control users cannot say the field name; everyone loses the hint once a placeholder disappears.

evidence.detail: Form elements must have labels: Fix any of the following:   Element does not have an implicit (wrapped) <label>
input[text] id=name name=name label="" placeholder="" required=true autocomplete="" NO-LABEL NO-AUTOCOMPLETE(name; 1.3.5) REQUIRED-NOT-SHOWN?(3.3.2: check visible cue)
Form elements must have labels: Fix any of the following:   Element does not have an implicit (wrapped) <label>
input[tel] id=phone name=phone label="" placeholder="" required=false autocomplete="" NO-LABEL NO-AUTOCOMPLETE(tel; 1.3.5)
input[email] id=email name=email label="" placeholder="Email" required=true autocomplete="" PLACEHOLDER-ONLY NO-AUTOCOMPLETE(email; 1.3.5) REQUIRED-NOT-SHOWN?(3.3.2: check visible cue)

remediation.summary: Form fields without a visible, programmatic label
steps: Give every input, select and textarea a visible <label for="id"> (placeholder text is not a label).
If the design hides the label, keep it in the DOM with a visually-hidden class, never display:none.
Group related controls (radio sets, date parts) in <fieldset> with a <legend>.

platforms.wordpress: Form plugin field settings: turn on "Show label" (Gravity Forms: Field label visibility; Contact Form 7: wrap the tag in <label>).
platforms.shopify: Theme code: sections/*.liquid or snippets for forms; add <label for> and keep the visually-hidden class.
platforms.webflow: Select the form field > Settings: add a Label element linked with the field ID.
platforms.framer: Use a Form component with label text, or an override that sets aria-labelledby to the visible text.
platforms.squarespace: Form block: every field has a label; do not leave it blank.
platforms.wix: Field settings > "Field title" (shown); avoid placeholder-only titles.
platforms.react: Render <label htmlFor={id}>; for design-system inputs require a `label` prop and fail the build without it.

remediation.verify: Click the label text: focus must move into the field. In DevTools > Accessibility the field's Name equals the visible label.

findings.title: Images missing a useful text alternative

impact.who: Blind users hear a file name or nothing at all, and miss product details, prices or link destinations.

evidence.detail: Images must have alternative text: Fix any of the following:   Element does not have an alt attribute
ALT-MISSING	img svg%3E alt=(none)
-	IMG-FILENAME(?)	no alt; real SR may say "svg%3E"

remediation.summary: Images missing a useful text alternative
steps: Informative image: alt describes what it conveys ("Red trail lantern, 300 lumens").
Decorative image: alt="" (empty), never missing.
Linked image: alt names the destination ("Trail lantern details").
Images of text: use real text, or put all the text in the alt.

platforms.wordpress: Media Library > image > Alternative Text; decorative: leave blank and the theme must output alt="".
platforms.shopify: Products > Media > Edit alt text; theme Liquid: {{ image | image_tag: alt: image.alt }}.
platforms.squarespace: Image block > Design/Content > Image alt text (filename is the default: replace it).
platforms.react: ; jsx-a11y/alt-text rule; CMS field required.

remediation.verify: Open the images review sheet (inventory *_images.html) and compare each alt to the picture; screen reader reads a meaningful phrase.

findings.title: Page changes on focus or input without warning

impact.who: Keyboard and screen-reader users are sent to a new page while just moving through a list or typing.

evidence.detail: CHANGE-ON-INPUT	select 0 "Shipping speed" ArrowDown -> GET http://127.0.0.1:4176/checkout-bad.html?ship=exp (3.2.2; aborted, not followed)
ONCHANGE-NAV?	select#ship "Standard Express Overnight" location.href='checkout-bad.html?ship='+this.value	(3.2.2 candidate; confirm below)

remediation.summary: Page changes on focus or input without warning
steps: Do not navigate on select change or on focus; add a "Go"/"Apply" button.
If a change must happen, explain it before the control.
remediation.verify: Arrow through each select and Tab across fields: nothing navigates or opens until you press the button.

2	NO-NAME	image

steps: Give icon-only controls a name: visible text, aria-label, or visually-hidden text.

platforms.shopify: Header cart/search icons in sections/header.liquid: add visually-hidden text.
platforms.webflow: Link block > Settings > Custom attribute aria-label.

impact.who: Low-vision users, older users and anyone on a phone in sunlight cannot read the text.

evidence.detail: Elements must meet minimum color contrast ratio thresholds: Fix any of the following:   Element has insufficient color contrast of 2.16 (foreground color: #b0b0b0, background color: #ffffff, font size: 12.0pt (16px), font weight: normal). Expected contrast ratio of 4.5:1
evidence.html: Free shipping on orders over $50. Prices include tax.

steps: Raise text contrast to at least 4.5:1 (3:1 for 24px+ or 18.66px+ bold text).
Fix the design token (brand colour) once rather than per element.
Check hover, focus and disabled-looking states too.

platforms.wordpress: Theme.json / Global Styles > Colors; Elementor Site Settings > Global Colors.
platforms.framer: Color styles in the Assets panel.
platforms.squarespace: Site Styles > Colors > edit the palette and section themes.
platforms.react: Design tokens; add a contrast check to the token pipeline.

remediation.verify: Measure with a contrast checker on the rendered pixels (not just CSS): 4.5:1 or better; re-run axe color-contrast.

impact.who: Screen readers read the text with the wrong voice and pronunciation.

remediation.summary: No working way to skip repeated navigation
steps: Make the first focusable element a "Skip to main content" link.
Point it at the main content: <main id="main" tabindex="-1">.
Keep it visible when focused (do not hide it with display:none).
remediation.after: Skip to main content ...

platforms.wordpress: Most block themes include one: check header.php or the theme's "skip link" option; make sure <main id> matches.
platforms.shopify: Dawn-based themes include `skip-to-content-link` in layout/theme.liquid; check the target id after customising.
platforms.webflow: Add a Link block first in the Navbar symbol pointing to a #main section ID; style it visible on focus.
platforms.framer: Add a link in the top layer pointing to the main section ID; set focus-visible styles.
platforms.squarespace: 7.1 sites include a "Skip to content" link: confirm it is the first Tab stop and lands on the main content; custom headers built in code blocks may need one added.
platforms.wix: Wix adds a "Skip to Main Content" link; confirm it appears first.
platforms.react: Render the skip link in the root layout and focus the <main> on route change.

remediation.verify: Load the page, press Tab once: the skip link appears; press Enter, then Tab: focus lands on the first item inside the main content.

findings.title: Page regions not marked up (no <main>, headings missing)

impact.who: Screen-reader users navigate by landmarks and headings; without them they must listen to the whole page.

locations.target: content sections use styled text, not headings (1.3.1, 2.4.6 "headings not programmatically determined")

evidence.detail: NO-REAL-HEADINGS	content sections use styled text, not headings (1.3.1, 2.4.6 "headings not programmatically determined")
NO-HEADINGS(2.4.1/1.3.1,medium)	no headings to navigate by
-	NO-HEADINGS

remediation.summary: Page regions not marked up (no <main>, headings missing)
steps: Wrap the primary content in one <main>; use <header>, <nav aria-label>, <footer>.
Give each page one <h1> and use real <h2>/<h3> headings for sections (not bold text).

platforms.wordpress: Block editor: use Heading blocks; theme template-parts should output <main>.
platforms.shopify: layout/theme.liquid: <main id="MainContent" role="main">; section titles as headings.
platforms.webflow: Set the element tag (Settings > Tag) to main/nav/header; use Heading elements.
platforms.framer: Set the HTML tag of frames (Accessibility > Tag) to main/nav; set text layers to H1/H2.
platforms.squarespace: Use Heading 1-4 text styles, not large paragraph text.
platforms.wix: Text settings: choose Heading 1-6 as the semantic tag (SEO & accessibility).
platforms.react: Layout component renders <main>; lint with eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y.

remediation.verify: Screen reader landmarks list (NVDA D / VoiceOver rotor) shows main and navigation; headings list reads as an outline of the page.

remediation.summary: Required fields shown by colour only (or not at all)
steps: Mark required fields in text: "(required)" in the label, or an asterisk explained at the top of the form.

platforms.wordpress: Form plugin: enable "Required" and the required indicator text.
platforms.shopify: Theme form snippet: add "(required)" text and the required attribute.
platforms.webflow: Field settings: check Required; add the text to the label.

findings.title: Click handler on an element keyboard users cannot reach

impact.who: Keyboard, switch and voice users cannot open the menu, accept the banner or press the button; the journey stops.

evidence.detail: MOUSE-ONLY	div.icon "" role=presentation	(2.1.1/4.1.2 candidate: not keyboard reachable)

remediation.summary: Controls that only work with a mouse
steps: Use native <button> for actions and <a href> for navigation; avoid clickable <div>/<span>.
If a custom control is unavoidable: tabindex="0", role, and Enter/Space handlers.
Menus must open on Enter/Space (and click), not only on hover.

platforms.wordpress: Replace page-builder "div with click action" widgets with Button widgets.
platforms.shopify: Theme JS: bind to <button>; for mega menus use <details>/<summary> or aria-expanded buttons.
platforms.webflow: Use Button or Link Block elements; Dropdown: enable "Open menu on hover" only alongside click/keyboard.
platforms.framer: Use Link/Button components; hover-only variants need a tap/focus trigger too.
platforms.squarespace: Built-in menus are keyboard accessible; custom code blocks need <button>.
platforms.wix: Use Button elements; Velo onClick on boxes is not keyboard accessible.
platforms.react: Use <button>; jsx-a11y rules click-events-have-key-events and no-static-element-interactions.

remediation.verify: Unplug the mouse: complete the journey with Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, arrows and Esc only.

conformance.statement: 16 candidate WCAG 2.2 Level A/AA failures (7 detected by deterministic automated rules, 9 needing human review) were found on the 1 page listed in Scope, using DOM inventory (language, headings, landmarks, images); automated rules (axe-core 4.14.0); a scripted keyboard Tab walk; form inspection (labels, autocomplete, required, client-side errors); reflow at 320 px and text-spacing checks; motion and reduced-motion checks; a simulated screen reader (Guidepup Virtual Screen Reader 0.33.0); context-change tests (focus and input); skip-link and reading-order checks, in headless Chromium (Playwright 1.65.1) at 390 px. No real screen reader (JAWS, NVDA, VoiceOver, TalkBack) and no testing with disabled users. Date: 2026-11-15. At least one rule-confirmed failure means these pages do not currently meet WCAG 2.2 AA. Do not describe the site as "compliant" or "conformant".

manualChecklist.check: On staging or with one owner-approved test entry: submit each journey form empty and with invalid values. Errors must be text, linked to the field, announced, and focus must move to them. Read-only runs cannot test server-side errors.
Complete every critical journey with the keyboard only (Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, arrows, Esc). Note any control you cannot reach, operate or leave.

Real screen reader pass on each journey: NVDA or JAWS with Chrome (Windows), VoiceOver with Safari (macOS and iOS), TalkBack with Chrome (Android). Listen to headings, landmarks, form labels, errors and status messages. Record AT, browser, OS and versions.
Judge alt text quality against the actual images (inventory *_images.html review sheet): does each alt convey what the image means here?
Check contrast of text over images, gradients and video, and of icons, input borders and focus rings, on rendered pixels.
Zoom to 200% and 400% in a real browser at 1280 px: nothing is cut off and no sideways scrolling for text content.
Instructions do not rely on shape, colour, size or position alone ("click the green button").
Hover/focus pop-ups (tooltips, menus) can be dismissed with Esc, hovered over, and stay until dismissed.
Voice control ("click Add to cart") works: accessible names start with the visible label.
Help and contact options appear in the same relative place on every page that has them.
Purchases, bookings and legal submissions can be reviewed, corrected or reversed before they are final.
Video and audio on journeys have accurate captions, transcripts and audio description where needed.
PDFs and documents linked from journeys are tagged and readable (or have an accessible HTML alternative).
Multi-step processes do not ask again for information already given.
Every drag action (sliders, sortable lists, maps) has a single-tap alternative.
